The Berkeley Beacon

Emerson’s film program ranks fifth in the country

By Katie Cressman, Editor-in-Chief / July 30, 2026
Share on Facebook
Share on X
Email this Story
zhihao wu
Students walk in front of The Colonial Building residence hall on Boylston St.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:59
Instaread

Rising over seven spots in just two years, Emerson College’s film program is now ranked fifth best in the country by The Hollywood Reporter.

It trails just behind film powerhouses including the University of Southern California and New York University, as well as the American Film Institute and Chapman University.  

The ranking, released July 24, cited Emerson’s “guiding principles on AI,” as part of the reason for its ranking, saying classes like AI and Media Production and Immersive Media in the AI Era help “students navigate their education with their individual levels of interest in the new tech in mind.” Chapman and NYU have also integrated AI into their curriculum, ranking second and fourth, respectively.

“We’re honored to be recognized among the top five film programs in the country” Interim Dean of the School of Film, Television, and Media Arts Shaun Clarke said. “Our broad-based curriculum gives students the freedom to experiment across genres, disciplines, and modalities, giving them an edge in today’s film, TV, and media landscape.”

The announcement also cited the appointment of Dean Ken Rogers to Emerson’s Los Angeles campus and the college’s plans to “expand everything from curriculum to early career support” at the satellite as reasons for its high ranking. 

Despite its Boston base, the outlet also acknowledged Emerson’s extensive alumni network in Hollywood, referencing co-chair and co-CEO of Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group Pam Abdy, Daniel Kwan, who directed Everything Everywhere All at Once alongside Emerson alum Daniel Scheinert, and screenwriter, producer, and Trustee Seth Grahame-Smith.

Grahame-Smith, the announcement said, will also award four film students with an annual, need-based scholarship which will last throughout the duration of their time at the college.

“The artists and creative storytellers coming out of Emerson College will continue to shape the industry in the years to come,” interim dean Clarke said.

Last year, the Hollywood Reporter ranked Emerson’s film program as the sixth best, and as 12th best in 2024, according to Emerson Today. 

About the Contributor
Katie Cressman, Editor-in-Chief
Katie Cressman is a senior journalism major from Bucks County, Pennsylvania, who serves as The Beacon’s Editor-in-Chief. Previously, Cressman worked as News Editor before taking a hiatus from The Beacon to complete a co-op on The Boston Globe’s copy desk. Following her co-op, Cressman worked as Projects Editor and Copy Chief at the Beacon while also working as a Messenger for the Globe. She is currently completing a second co-op on the Globe’s Homepage. On campus, she is the Vice President for Xi Gamma Nu and sings in Achoired Taste. To keep up with Cressman and her reporting, visit her website, read her USA Today and Boston Globe coverage or connect with her on LinkedIn.
